Historical source interfaces remain qualified for the 86 tail-call wrappers and 68 return-only functions, even where current caller/shared-header evidence supports the selected contract. A return-only function is not proved unused, and void(void) is not proof of its old signature. Byte equality of a tail branch cannot waive positive pointer, const, callback or floating-input evidence. All five c004 signature defects were checked in the corrected wrapper and receiving declarations and are resolved; the preserved-null-dereference publication gap is also resolved. func_00122510 has a supported void contract for the known direct caller, but return use by unknown indirect consumers remains [INFERENCE].

Header linkage, output-pointer depth, widths, signedness and the used virtual slots agree with the visible uses. This is not a complete C++ type/const checker, heap-alias proof or recovery of concrete virtual classes; source record views remain partial.

func_001470c8 correctly passes the manager lock at +0x1c4, but its local ManagerLock/ObjectManager definitions are partial prefixes rather than proven full extents (the receiver also accesses lock+4/+8). No allocation, sizeof, copy or array-stride use of these local partial definitions was found. The array-destroy callback pointer-return convention is compatible with the selected source contract; the return-only body alone does not prove a callback-result requirement.
